title: Waiting for the film
objective: Recognize tension pneumothorax as a clinical diagnosis treated before imaging

brief.situation: 17:05 in the emergency department. You are the nurse in a trauma room. Mr. Reyes, 29, came off his bicycle onto the curb and has left-sided chest pain. He is talking in sentences.
handover: Triage: ESI 2. Heart rate 108, respiratory rate 24, SpO2 94% on room air, blood pressure 128/80. Tender left ribs, breath sounds slightly reduced on the left.
The physician has ordered oxygen, a portable chest x-ray (coming in about 20 minutes) and IV access, and wants to know at once about any change in breathing or blood pressure.
The decompression kit is in the room.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assess and treat as you think the patient needs. Each assessment takes the time on its button.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Mr. Reyes is gasping and his pressure is falling. What is happening, and what do you do?

parts.label: What is happening
parts.criteria: Absent breath sounds on the injured side, tracheal deviation, distended neck veins, hypotension and tachycardia after chest trauma are tension pneumothorax.
parts.modelAnswer: He has a tension pneumothorax: silent left chest, trachea pushed right, distended neck veins, and now hypotension and falling saturation after a chest injury.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Physician to the bedside now for needle decompression without waiting for the x-ray; kit ready; stay with him, oxygen on; hand off.
parts.modelAnswer: Get the physician now to decompress; it's a clinical diagnosis, so we don't wait for the film. The kit is open, he stays on high-flow oxygen, and I hand off the times.

worsened.headline: Arrest from tension

wrongRoute.body: Waiting for imaging is the classic error. The physician decompresses on the clinical signs.

scoring.modelReasoning: A rib injury with reduced breath sounds can become a tension pneumothorax. Oxygen and access go in at once, the kit is opened, and he is reassessed often. When breath sounds disappear, the trachea shifts, neck veins distend and the pressure falls, it is tension: a clinical diagnosis. The physician decompresses at the bedside without waiting for the x-ray.

dxQ.ask: While you assess: how is tension pneumothorax diagnosed in an unstable patient?
dxQ.explain: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis; in an unstable patient needle decompression comes without delay, and imaging only if stable.
